Workstream 02 · NEOS Item Tracker (Blazor → React Port) v5 merged to main · v6/v7 dev branches

Agentic legacy-to-React migration from structured sources of truth.

Developed an agentic approach to porting NEOS's Item Tracker from the legacy Blazor application into a React-based frontend. Structured the repository so coding agents work from three explicit sources of truth: legacy code for business behaviour and API contracts, the prototype for visual design and interactions, and architecture documentation for implementation patterns.

  • Shell demo & iterative branches: Built the initial Item Tracker demo inside the navigation shell, merged v5 into main, and extended v6 and v7 development branches with tested workflows for saved views, bulk CSV filtering, grid behaviour, quick views, item details, exports, and theming.
  • Performance & test coverage: Isolated overlay state, deferred expensive filtering passes, and added automated tests around evolving interactions and data models (keeping v6/v7 clearly scoped as development-branch iterations rather than a claimed production release).
Workstream 03 · Reusable Agent Skills & Hill-Climbing Review Loop Automated evidence PRs

Turning agent failure modes into repeatable engineering verification gates.

Designed reusable agent skills and repository guidance so other developers and future NEOS modules can repeat the workflow—guiding agents through legacy behaviour tracing, prototype state comparison, performance investigation, and automated formatted PRs with meaningful evidence that cut review time.

  • Iterative hill-climbing review loop: Created a review-loop skill that runs independent agent reviews to surface defects, apply fixes, and re-verify rather than accepting the first implementation.
  • Live interaction & rendered-font gates: After an early prototype-matching pass missed search focus and typography subtleties, documented the failure and hardened the skill to require live browser interaction checks, rendered-font evidence, and honest reporting of unverified differences.
